### Known gaps

- OPEN 2026-09-07 (gopherstack-z1sd triage): StartPipelineExecution (pipelines.go) sets PipelineExecutionStatus directly to pipelineStatusSucceeded and returns -- it never goes through pipelineStatusExecuting at all, and there is no runDelayed call. This is inconsistent with its own siblings in the same package: RetryPipelineExecution and StopPipelineExecution (pipeline_executions.go) both set an intermediate status (Executing/Stopping) then use the existing b.runDelayed(b.lifecycleCtx, ...) mechanism to transition to the terminal status (Succeeded/Stopped) after a short delay (retryTransitionDelay/stopTransitionDelay), matching the real PipelineExecutionStatus enum (sagemaker@v1.263.2 types/enums.go:6945-6954: Executing/Stopping/Stopped/Failed/Succeeded). So this is NOT a case of an unreachable-by-construction status (contrast the docdb/neptune snapshot-status findings elsewhere in this triage pass) -- the async-transition infrastructure already exists in this exact file and is already used correctly by two sibling ops; StartPipelineExecution alone skips it. Fix is a small, local, well-precedented change: mirror RetryPipelineExecution's pattern (set pipelineStatusExecuting, Put, then runDelayed to flip to pipelineStatusSucceeded). Not attempted this pass (triage only, no .go writes).
- Pagination across the service is a hand-rolled integer-offset NextToken (parseNextToken/strconv.Atoi) rather than pkgs/page's opaque-token helper. Functionally correct (AWS clients treat NextToken as opaque) and internally consistent, but is a pkgs-catalog convention deviation across ~15 call sites. Not fixed this pass — refactor is cross-cutting and out of budget for a single-family sweep. (no bd issue filed yet)

Sufficient for status-polling clients; deeper fidelity deferred. (no bd issue filed yet)
